title: R. Vale — can Doubt preserve unresolved identity and attributed contradiction?
question: Do the identical Programme A and Catalogue B strings, plus Source C's statement, settle whether the two R. Vale mentions refer to one maker or two?
verdict: No. The one-maker/two-maker world remains unresolved; Source C is attributable contrary evidence and should not be upgraded into a directly observed identity fact.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: Identity remains unresolved; Source C supplies a reported contradiction to the one-maker hypothesis, not direct observation.

nodes.label: Two live identity worlds
nodes.text: The preserved outside case explicitly states that identical strings are consistent with either one maker or two makers.

nodes.label: Attributed Source C statement
nodes.text: The preserved case says Source C reports that programme A's R. Vale is not catalogue B's maker and must remain attributed.

nodes.label: Actual referent identity
nodes.text: Whether the two original mentions actually refer to one maker or two remains unknown.

nodes.label: Source C correctness
nodes.text: The correctness of Source C's reported distinction is not established by the synthetic case itself.

edges.note: The source explicitly says the two original strings alone cannot decide between one-maker and two-maker worlds.
Source C changes the evidence state but remains a report rather than direct observation of identity.
The unresolved hidden-world identity blocks a definitive entity-resolution claim.
The source-attributed contradiction cannot be promoted to observed fact without independent evidence.
